### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 each ran in roughly a third of the cases (about 71, 61 and 70 of 200 traces, i.e. about 36%, 31% and 35%); in the later window A19 and A25 appear in none of 200 traces and A20 in only 1. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- These three were mutually exclusive alternatives: in the earlier window each pair almost never co-occurred (at most about 1 in 200 traces), while together they covered essentially every trace (shares summing to about 100 in 100). [REL007, REL009, REL014, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- The block sat between A41 and A26: about 93 in 100 of A41's outgoing transitions went to one of the three (roughly a third to each), about 97–99 in 100 of the outgoing transitions of A19, A20 and A25 went to A26, and relationally A41 came before each of the three, and each before A26, in about 30–35% of traces. [DIR004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL012, REL017, REL021, REL010, REL015, REL019]
- In the later window, A41 leads directly to A26 in about 92 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously essentially never observed), and A26 occurs in essentially every trace without any of the three. [DIR004, REL010, REL015, REL019]
- Small relative event-position shifts accompany this: A26's mean relative position moved slightly earlier (about 0.39 to 0.37) while A41's and A14's moved slightly later (about 0.32 to 0.33 and 0.14 to 0.15); these are event positions, not clock times. [POS005, POS006, POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the three-way alternative block A19/A20/A25 that previously always ran between A41 and A26 is skipped: A41 now leads directly to A26, and the three activities are no longer executed in this segment. The participation drop is direct (0 of 200 later traces for A19 and A25, 1 of 200 for A20), the rewiring is shown directly in A41's outgoing transitions (about 93% into the block before versus about 92% straight to A26 after), and the relational items place A41 before the block and the block before A26 in the earlier window while showing A41 and A26 without them later. With 34 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.6 expected by chance, this set of differences is not what an unchanged process typically produces, and all items describe one coherent difference rather than scattered effects. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR004, REL012, REL017, REL021, REL010, REL015, REL019]

Limitations: zero participation strictly means "not observed", so very rare persistence of the three activities cannot be excluded, and the many relational items largely re-express the same trace behaviour rather than confirming it independently; the small position shifts of A14, A41 and A26 are consistent side effects of shorter traces, not separate changes. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, POS001, POS005, POS006]

Other differences: the single later occurrence of A20 appears at a later relative position (about 0.62 versus about 0.36 before) and its one observed outgoing edge leads to A30 instead of A26; based on one trace, this cannot show whether A20 survives anywhere else in the process. [POS003, DIR002]

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the three activities still occur below observable frequency, or that the segment was replaced by behaviour outside the tested units; the later window shows no occurrence in 200 traces but cannot prove complete removal. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
